tone_statements.citation: 鈴木博之 (Suzuki, Hiroyuki). 2023. [書評] 宋成、謝穎瑩、李大勤、李佐文（著）《西藏察隅松林語》北京：商務印書館、2019 年、10+272pp. 言語記述論集 (Journal of Kijutsuken, Descriptive Linguistics Study Group) 15: 75-84. 言語記述研究会.
tone_statements.quote: • 音節声調で、３つの対立がある本書の分析では、音節ごとに声調を認め、55、24、31 の３種が対立することになっている。注意すべきは複音節語の構成要素になったとき変調することがあるという指摘（p.24）で、変化しないか 33 か 31 と記述する。[...] 本書では声調に文法的機能があると述べ（p. 25）、31 調が主に機能語に現れるという観察を提示している。一方で格標識は 55 調で固定されているということで、特徴的である。
tone_statements.translation: • Syllable tone, with three contrasts. In the book's analysis a tone is recognised on every syllable, and three kinds, 55, 24 and 31, contrast. Noteworthy is the remark (p. 24) that a syllable may change tone when it becomes a constituent of a polysyllabic word: it is described as either unchanged, or 33, or 31. [...] The book states that tone has a grammatical function (p. 25) and offers the observation that tone 31 appears mainly on function words, while case markers are fixed at tone 55, which is distinctive.
tone_statements.locator: pp.78-79, §3.1 音声・音韻について, '声調体系について注目すべき点'
tone_statements.summary: Three syllable tones (55 high level, 24 rising, 31 falling) per Song et al. 2019, with sandhi in polysyllables (unchanged/33/31), an intonational 42 on interrogatives, and a grammatical skew (31 mostly on function words, case markers fixed 55); reviewer proposes a Tibetic-style word-tone re-analysis.

tone_statements.citation: 鈴木博之 (Suzuki, Hiroyuki). 2023. 松林語におけるチベット系借用語の性質について / Characteristics of Tibetic Loanwords in the Songlin Language. 東京大学言語学論集 Tokyo University Linguistic Papers 45 (eTULIP, 2023.10): e1-e41. 東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科・文学部言語学研究室. doi:10.15083/0002008127; hdl:2261/0002008127.
tone_statements.quote: なお、宋成 等(2019:18–33)による松林語の音体系および表記に用いられる音標文字は次のようである。[...] 超分節音素：55, 24, 31。 [...] 蔵文鼻音字類の音対応について見ると、表５に示すように、鼻音字が単独である場合は原則的に有声鼻音かつ低声調で現れ、鼻音字に s 以外の先行子音字がある場合は有声鼻音かつ高声調で現れ、鼻音字に s が先行する場合は無声鼻音かつ高声調で現れる。
tone_statements.translation: The sound system of Songlin and the phonetic symbols used in transcription according to Song et al. (2019:18-33) are as follows. [...] Suprasegmental phonemes: 55, 24, 31. [...] Looking at the correspondences of the Written Tibetan nasal letters, as Table 5 shows, when the nasal letter stands alone it appears in principle as a voiced nasal with low tone; when the nasal letter has a pre-initial letter other than s it appears as a voiced nasal with high tone; and when s precedes the nasal letter it appears as a voiceless nasal with high tone.
tone_statements.locator: p.e2 (§1, inventory) and p.e5 (§2.1, Table 5 蔵文鼻音字類の音対応); also p.e14 (§2.2: no vowel length, no tone-length relation)
tone_statements.summary: Three tones 55 / 24 / 31 taken over from Song et al. 2019; in Tibetic loans the high vs low (55 vs 24/31) register correlates with Written Tibetan onset type (pre-initials give high register on sonorants), no tone-length interaction.

sources.note: Restates the Songlin phoneme inventory from Song et al. 2019:18-33 with 'suprasegmental phonemes: 55, 24, 31' (p.e2), cites every Songlin form with its tone, and gives tone-register correspondences in the Tibetic loan layer, e.g. Written Tibetan plain nasal initials -> voiced nasal + LOW tone, nasals with a pre-initial other than s -> voiced nasal + HIGH tone, s+nasal -> voiceless nasal + HIGH tone (p.e5, Table 5); also notes that Songlin has no vowel-length contrast and no relation between tone and syllable length (p.e14). A tonogenetically informative first-hand comparative treatment.
